items.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011
items.q: he studied with Sir Richard Thomas Beecham, orchestration.

ctx.x: Well after I left Jimmy Cavallo’s band, the bass player and I actually left together and formed a trio, and we picked up a drummer in Atlantic City where we were working, his name was Jack Toker, a wonderful drummer. And Jack and I and the bass player had a © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -5-

group for about six months and that fell apart and I said okay, I decided I was going to come home, and the drummer said he was going to stay out on the road. Well he hooked up with a show band at that time, and this must have been ’69, ’70, right around that time. There were lots of gigs and so you could play the Holiday Inn circuit, you could keep working, again, covering songs on the radio, this stuff. So he got into a group that was pretty good about this, and they were all over the country. So he happened to…

arrogant. And he was always breaking my chops because we said my friend Jack Toker is playing with Lou Rawls and I got a postcard from them and they’re going to be going to Europe. Oh wonderful. And so he would always say things to me like “well gee maybe Lou Rawls is going to call you up to play this gig in Frankfort” or something like that. And I said “well that’d be nice.” And so one time we were rehearsing and the phone rings. And he said “hey answer that it’s probably Lou Rawls.” And it was. And I said oh…
